key_insight: Wan-Dancer introduces a hierarchical generation framework that can produce minute-scale dance videos synchronized to music, pushing beyond the short-duration limits of typical diffusion-based video models. It aims to keep motion coherent, identity consistent, and rhythm aligned over much longer time horizons.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of generating long-duration, high-definition music-to-dance videos without temporal drift, identity inconsistency, or repetitive motion breakdowns that commonly appear in existing methods after about 20 seconds.
method: Uses a hierarchical framework to break long dance generation into manageable temporal units while preserving global coherence.
Targets coherent music-to-dance synchronization over minute-scale durations rather than only short clips.
Designed to reduce common failure modes in long video synthesis, including drift, repeated motion, and appearance inconsistency.
impact: This matters for practitioners because it moves music-conditioned video generation closer to practical long-form content creation. The approach may inform future systems for controllable, temporally stable video synthesis in entertainment, virtual avatars, and creative tools.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing the hierarchical generation stages from music input to final dance video.
A timeline comparison illustrating short-segment drift vs. minute-scale coherent motion.
Side-by-side frames highlighting identity consistency and rhythmic alignment over time.
An error-mode panel showing temporal drift, repetition, and inconsistency in prior methods versus Wan-Dancer.
paper_title: Wan-Dancer: A Hierarchical Framework for Minute-scale Coherent Music-to-Dance Generation
paper_authors: Mingyang Huang, Peng Zhang, Li Hu, Guangyuan Wang, Bang Zhang
